name: eiapy
what_it_holds: Python client wrapping the full EIA Open Data API v2 (222 leaf routes across 13 categories: petroleum, natural gas, electricity, coal, SEDS, STEO, AEO/IEO, etc.), returning typed pandas DataFrames. Petroleum category includes get_data("petroleum","pri","gnd") for retail gasoline/diesel prices (EIA's weekly/monthly regional and national gas price series). Requires a free EIA API key (no payment).
why_useful: One-command, no-cost, no-scraping pull of EIA's official weekly/monthly retail gasoline and diesel price series (by PADD region and US average), which is the standard non-AAA benchmark for consumer fuel cost and a clean point-in-time-able macro input; also opens EIA's much broader petroleum/energy dataset (jet fuel, refinery data) relevant to travel-cost gap analyses.
time_coverage: as far back as EIA series go (gasoline weekly since 1990s) via the API
size_hint: API client, no committed data; pull volume depends on query
last_activity: recent, under active development per README
themes: Road travel and fuel: gas prices (EIA, AAA), vehicle miles travelled, holiday driving, toll data
why_all: One-command, no-cost, no-scraping pull of EIA's official weekly/monthly retail gasoline and diesel price series (by PADD region and US average), which is the standard non-AAA benchmark for consumer fuel cost and a clean point-in-time-able macro input; also opens EIA's much broader petroleum/energy dataset (jet fuel, refinery data) relevant to travel-cost gap analyses.

name: GoogleTrendsAnchorBank (gtab)
what_it_holds: Python package `gtab` implementing the anchor-bank calibration method from the CIKM 2020 paper 'Calibration of Google Trends Time Series' (Robert West, EPFL). Directories: gtab/ (core library), example/ (notebooks + CLI demos), cikm2020_paper/ (reproducibility materials). Builds a set of calibration ('anchor') queries so arbitrary Google Trends queries can be placed on one absolute, comparable scale instead of the 0-100 relative index that changes with every pull. Pulls live via pytrends; does not ship pre-built historical data but the anchor-bank building code is a one-command pipeline. MIT license, 217 commits.
why_useful: Directly targets gap #17 (anchored Google Trends, gtab named explicitly) and gap #4 (point-in-time Google Trends). Our own Trends work failed 0/162 vs naive partly on renormalisation; this is the standard academic fix others (including the OECD Weekly Tracker methodology) build on, so worth testing before concluding Trends is dead.
last_activity: unknown exact date; 217 commits, actively cited
time_coverage: user-defined (as far back as Trends allows)
size_hint: small library, no large data files

name: trendecon
what_it_holds: R package that queries Google Trends at multiple frequencies (daily/weekly/monthly) for the same terms and harmonises them into a single consistent daily index, preserving long-run trend levels that a single Trends pull cannot give (Trends caps daily granularity to short windows). Companion site trendecon.org publishes daily-updated Swiss economic indicators built this way. Published in Economic Inquiry (2022). No committed data files -- data pulled on demand via gtrendsR. GPL-3.0, 41 stars, grew out of a 2020 COVID hackathon.
why_useful: This is essentially a from-scratch, open-source recipe for building an OECD-Weekly-Tracker-style consistent daily/weekly Google Trends series -- addresses the same renormalisation problem that killed our 0/162 Trends test. Could be re-run for US/EMEA travel-adjacent search terms instead of the 9 terms we already tried.
geography: primarily Switzerland demo; geo parameter is configurable

name: FRBNY Nowcasting (dynamic factor model)
what_it_holds: New York Fed's own MATLAB implementation of the dynamic-factor-model nowcasting framework from their Staff Report 830 ('Macroeconomic Nowcasting and Forecasting with Big Data') -- the same family of methodology underlying the NY Fed / now-Dallas-Fed Weekly Economic Index. Ships example US data pulled from FRED, a model-spec template, and a pre-computed DFM results file, but explicitly does NOT include the full proprietary dataset used for the live weekly release (redistribution restricted). BSD-3-Clause, 4 commits visible.
why_useful: Not a data source, but it is the actual official mixed-frequency DFM code the WEI/GDP nowcast family is built on -- useful if we want to build our own weekly ABNB-demand nowcast (gap #17, MIDAS/DFM nowcasting) rather than only tracking someone else's published index.

name: alfred (R package, CRAN)
what_it_holds: R client for ALFRED (Archival FRED) that pulls historical data releases / vintages for any FRED series with no API key required; returns tidy data frames of a series as it was known at any given past date. Example series shown: INDPRO. On CRAN since June 2017, last functional update 26 Jul 2021; mirrored at github.com/cran/alfred (0 stars, but that's just the CRAN read-only mirror).
why_useful: Directly implements gap #4 (ALFRED-style macro vintages). Gives point-in-time snapshots of any FRED series (GDP, PCE, CPI, payrolls, industrial production) as they stood on a given historical date -- exactly what's needed to refit at guide dates per the repo's point-in-time rule rather than using today's revised macro series as an input to nowcasts of consumer spend/travel demand.
time_coverage: Whatever vintage history FRED/ALFRED expose per series (many series back to 1990s-2000s vintages)
size_hint: small R package, no committed data (live API pulls)
themes: Point-in-time macro vintages: ALFRED tooling, Philly Fed real-time dataset, ONS revisions, Eurostat vintages; packages for vintage-aware backtests
why_all: Directly implements gap #4 (ALFRED-style macro vintages).
